sourcedFrom: SAFETY AND OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — Semi-Automatic Sport Pistol Cal. .380 Auto — rev. C (UNKNOWN — no copyright line printed; the back cover dates the revision to December 2009)
cleanIntro: The PK380 is a hammer-fired SA/DA .380 Auto with a manual safety, eight rounds, a 93 mm barrel — and a keyed lock in the left side of the frame that is part of the takedown, not just a storage feature. You cannot field strip this pistol without its key. Walther publishes one disassembly step for it and nothing beyond, so this is a short, well-bounded procedure with an unusual first move.

steps.title: Find the key before you start
steps.action: Locate the key supplied with the pistol. On the PK380 that key turns a lock in the left side of the frame which locks the trigger mechanism — and the same lock has to be turned to get the slide off. Without the key this pistol does not field strip.
steps.prose: This is the first thing to establish because it is the thing that stops the job dead. The lock's ordinary purpose is safe storage: a quarter turn counter-clockwise locks the trigger mechanism and the pistol cannot be opened without the key, which greatly reduces the risk of use by an unauthorised person. But the takedown uses the same lock at a different angle, so a PK380 whose key has been lost is a pistol that cleans from the outside only. Confirm the chambering while you are looking: .380 Auto, also marked 9 mm Browning short, eight rounds, SA/DA.
steps.aside: Locked is a quarter turn counter-clockwise; unlocked is a quarter turn clockwise. The 135 degrees used for takedown is a different position again.
steps.quote: Use the supplied key to lock the trigger mechanism of the PK380 (fig. 3).
steps.cite: SAFETY AND OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — Semi-Automatic Sport Pistol Cal. .380 Auto — rev. C — 1.2 Trigger lock, printed p.03 (PDF p.3)

steps.title: Safety to SAFE, magazine out
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction. Rotate the safety lever to the lower position, which is SAFE. Then depress the magazine catch and remove the magazine.
steps.prose: The PK380 has a real manual safety and this is one of the few modern Walthers where the clearing procedure starts with it — lever down is safe, lever up is fire, and the manual's own line is to leave it engaged until you intend to fire. Set it before anything else moves. The magazine catch is at the base of the trigger guard and an eight-round .380 magazine is light enough to need catching. Empty the magazine by pushing each cartridge forward out of the lips, not by levering them upward.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine, pull back the slide and make sure that the chamber is empty.
steps.cite: SAFETY AND OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — Semi-Automatic Sport Pistol Cal. .380 Auto — rev. C — 2 Inspection, printed p.05 (PDF p.5)
steps.warn: Grip the slide from above or from the back when pulling it. Never put your hand in front of the muzzle.

steps.title: Slide back, chamber checked, and the barrel looked through
steps.action: Grip the slide from above or from behind — never in front of the muzzle — draw it fully back so that any round in the chamber is ejected, and look into the chamber. Then make a visual inspection down the barrel and confirm it is clear.
steps.prose: The PK380's slide has a small slot above the extractor that shows whether a round is in the chamber, which is useful and is not a substitute for looking. That indicator is a mechanical feature and Walther's instruction is never to rely solely on mechanical features. The pistol has no slide-lock-on-empty behaviour to hold the slide open for you during inspection, so hold it back yourself while you look. The barrel check matters on a .380 that may have been stored oiled.
steps.quote: A small slot above the extractor allows inspection of the chamber to see if there is a round in the chamber (fig. 6a) or not (fig. 6b).
steps.cite: SAFETY AND OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — Semi-Automatic Sport Pistol Cal. .380 Auto — rev. C — 1.4 Loaded chamber indicator, printed p.04 (PDF p.4)
steps.warn: Make a visual inspection of the barrel — it must be clear.

steps.title: Decock the hammer, thumb on it the whole way
steps.action: With the muzzle in a safe direction, engage the safety and remove the magazine. Pull back the slide and make sure the chamber is empty. Then aim in a safe direction, release the safety, hold the hammer with your thumb, pull the trigger and let the hammer travel slowly forward.
steps.prose: This is a manual decock on a hammer-fired pistol, so your thumb is the only thing between a controlled lowering and a dropped hammer — take a firm hold before the trigger moves, and let it down in one continuous motion rather than in stages. Note the order Walther gives: safety on and magazine out FIRST, chamber verified, and only then is the safety released so the trigger can move. The safety has to come off because the trigger will not operate through it. Keep the pistol pointed somewhere safe throughout; this is the same motion that fires the gun.
steps.quote: Point the pistol in a safe direction. Engage the safety and remove the magazine. Pull back the slide and make sure that the chamber is empty (fig. 13). Aim in a safe direction and release the safety. While holding the hammer with your thumb, pull the trigger and let the hammer slowly move forward.
steps.cite: SAFETY AND OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — Semi-Automatic Sport Pistol Cal. .380 Auto — rev. C — 6 Decocking the hammer, printed p.07 (PDF p.7)
steps.warn: Keep the pistol pointing in a safe direction when decocking. Failure to do this can result in serious injury or death.

steps.title: Decocked, safety on, magazine out — confirm all three
steps.action: Before touching the lock: confirm the hammer is down, the safety is engaged, the magazine is out, and the pistol is not loaded.
steps.prose: Walther puts these four conditions together as a single precondition for disassembly, and on a hammer-fired pistol they are not redundant with one another — a decocked PK380 with the safety off is still a gun whose trigger works, and a safe PK380 with a magazine in it is one movement from loaded. Run through them in order and physically check each rather than recalling it. This is also the last moment before the key goes into the frame, and once that lock is turned the pistol is committed to coming apart.
steps.caution: Always follow the disassembly instructions exactly. Never do anything beyond what you are specifically instructed to do in this manual. Never alter or modify the parts in your firearm.
steps.quote: Before disassembling the pistol, decock it and lock the safety. Remove the magazine and make sure that the pistol is not loaded.
steps.cite: SAFETY AND OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — Semi-Automatic Sport Pistol Cal. .380 Auto — rev. C — 10 Disassembling and assembling the pistol, printed p.09 (PDF p.9)

steps.title: Key in, 135 degrees counter-clockwise, takedown lever straight down
steps.action: Put the key into the lock on the LEFT side of the pistol and turn it counter-clockwise by 135 degrees. Then pull the takedown lever straight down. Slowly draw the slide, with the barrel in it, forward off the frame.
steps.prose: One hundred and thirty-five degrees is three-eighths of a turn, well past the quarter turn used for the trigger lock, and the lever will not move until the key has gone the whole way — a lever that feels solid means the key is short of position, not that the pistol is seized. Pull the lever straight down rather than swinging it; it is a slide, not a pivot. The slide and barrel then come off the front together as one unit and there is nothing to arrest them, so control the movement with the hand behind, never in front of the muzzle. Assembly is exactly these steps reversed.
steps.quote: To remove the slide, use the key to turn the lock on the left side of the pistol counter-clockwise by 135° (fig. 14). Pull the takedown lever straight down (fig. 15). Slowly pull off the slide with the barrel (fig. 16).
steps.cite: SAFETY AND OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — Semi-Automatic Sport Pistol Cal. .380 Auto — rev. C — 10 Disassembling and assembling the pistol, printed p.09 (PDF p.9)
steps.warn: The lock is on the LEFT side of the frame and the takedown angle is 135°, not the 90° used to lock and unlock the trigger mechanism.

steps.title: The key stays in until the pistol is back together
steps.action: Leave the key in the lock while the pistol is apart. It cannot be withdrawn while the lock is open — reassemble the pistol and lock it before the key will come out.
steps.prose: This is deliberate, not a fault, and it is the PK380's built-in reminder that the pistol is not finished. Because the key is captive with the lock open, you cannot walk away from a half-stripped PK380 with the key in your pocket, and you cannot mislay it mid-clean. It does mean the key sits sticking out of the frame throughout the job, so keep it where it will not be knocked and bent. Do not try to force it out; the lock will simply not release it.
steps.quote: The key cannot be removed when the lock is open. To remove the key, one must first assemble the pistol and lock it.
steps.cite: SAFETY AND OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — Semi-Automatic Sport Pistol Cal. .380 Auto — rev. C — 10 Disassembling and assembling the pistol, printed p.09 (PDF p.9)

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, and the slide with the barrel in it. That is the entire disassembly Walther publishes for the PK380 — the barrel is not separated from the slide and no internal group comes out.
steps.prose: Two assemblies is the whole of it, and the manual's warranty terms make the boundary explicit: disassembly beyond the field stripping instructions in this manual is excluded from cover. Everything the cleaning section asks for is reachable from here — the breech, the barrel, the magazine lips and follower, and the frame. If the pistol is not functioning properly after cleaning, that is a gunsmith's job, not a deeper strip. Reassembly is these steps in reverse, and the key comes out only once the pistol is together and locked.
steps.quote: Only an authorized and qualified gunsmith should inspect and repair your firearm!
steps.cite: SAFETY AND OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — Semi-Automatic Sport Pistol Cal. .380 Auto — rev. C — 14 Repairs, printed p.10 (PDF p.10)

deepAbsentReason: Walther's PK380 book publishes exactly one disassembly step — key to 135°, takedown lever down, slide-with-barrel off the frame — and nothing past it. The barrel is never separated from the slide, no slide internals are documented, and the magazine is emptied but never stripped. Section 14 sends any further work to an authorised and qualified gunsmith, and the warranty in section 15 explicitly excludes defects arising from disassembly beyond the field stripping instructions in this manual. There is no deeper published procedure to walk, so none is invented here.

cleaning.name: BARREL & BREECH
tasks: Clean the barrel with an oil-soaked brush and then dry it with cleaning patches — always begin at the CHAMBER end
Repeat until the barrel is clean; .380 lead residue in a 93 mm barrel takes more than one pass
Remove fouling from the breech with a brush and a cloth
Dry-patch the bore before the pistol is loaded — oil standing in the chamber raises pressure

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE & FRAME
tasks: Brush and cloth on the magazine lips and the follower — the two places a .380 feed problem usually starts
Remove fouling from the frame with a brush and a cloth; do not disassemble the magazine, the book does not publish it
Empty the magazine by pushing each cartridge forward out of the lips, never by levering upward

cleaning.name: OIL & FUNCTION
tasks: Apply a thin coat of oil to all metal parts using only high-quality gun oil
Reassemble the pistol and check it for proper function before it goes away
Clean and maintain at regular intervals rather than only after firing — Walther frames this as service-life maintenance
Wipe the key and the lock face; grit in that lock is what makes a PK380 takedown feel stiff

cleaning.name: BEFORE IT GOES AWAY
tasks: Store unloaded, with the safety in the safe position, and the trigger mechanism locked with the key
Keep pistol and ammunition away from children and unauthorized persons, and store them separately
A firearm which fails to function properly is dangerous: store it in a way that prevents its use until it is repaired

reassembly: Slide with barrel back onto the frame rails from the front, pushed fully to the rear.
Push the takedown lever back up into its seated position.
Turn the key clockwise back through 135° to close the lock, then withdraw the key — it will not come out until the pistol is assembled and locked.
Set the manual safety to the SAFE (lower) position.
Check the rear sight is still tight on its pin; windage is set by moving the rear sight left or right, so a knock during cleaning shifts the zero.
Function-check before the pistol is loaded: slide fully forward, hammer down, safety operating between lower and upper positions.
fncheck: With the magazine out and the chamber confirmed empty: remove the magazine, pull the slide back, confirm the chamber is empty and let the slide run all the way forward. Insert the empty magazine and pull the slide back — it should be held in its rearmost position by the slide stop. Remove the magazine, pull the slide back slightly and release it; it must close all the way. Then check the safety: lever down should block the trigger, lever up should free it. Confirm the takedown lever is fully seated and the frame lock is closed with the key withdrawn — a PK380 that still has its key in the frame is not assembled. Finally confirm the hammer is down and the safety is set to SAFE before the pistol is stored.
